headline: Nine AI labs disclosed an October API-key swarming; 20VC flags million-dollar theft bills

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's three minutes to midnight UTC on Thursday, November twelfth. This is ARA AI News. The security story just moved from OpenAI's scanning tools to a wave of stolen A P I keys.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On twenty VC, a guest said nine of the leading A I developers disclosed a swarming incident in October alone.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The same conversation cited Unit 42 saying bills hit one million dollars before anyone caught the theft.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: A guest said their own Ultra spend on Claude was set at one hundred thousand dollars by default, and that a stolen Fireworks key could burn that cap in minutes.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: They said crime syndicates steal Anthropic and OpenAI tokens. That lands on top of this afternoon's OpenAI guides for Daybreak Blue and automated GitHub reviews.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Twenty VC also tied the Nvidia spy case to where the chips actually sit.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: A guest said it is unfortunate that inference and G P U chips for China-based models are hosted in Singapore and Thailand, even beyond the alleged spy story.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: They argued China loses here. Selling G P U chips into China and hosting them just across the border will get shut down, they said, and a measure had already passed the House and stalled in the Senate.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: On the spending selloff, a guest said this does not follow from Nvidia losing share to A M D. If demand shows up in OpenAI's annual recurring revenue, everything else is roughly fine.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: The test they flagged is token price. A ten to twenty percent cut only lifts revenue if usage rises about twenty-one percent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: If usage rises fifteen percent, net revenue falls. They said the basis of competition is compute capital and token pricing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That sits beside CoreWeave's breakout quarter and the earlier claim that Anthropic and OpenAI ramps already beat the nineteen nineties internet buildout.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: On lab funding, a guest said people talk about one point four trillion dollars versus one trillion because a private valuation counts all the options, and that per share value is up about twenty to thirty percent.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: They also said a trillion-dollar allocator was not worried about this eighty billion dollars, but about the next hundred billion, because that layer is very thin.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Kalshi's December I P O odds and the November nineteenth watch still stand. What to watch next is whether any lab confirms the October swarming by name, and whether Anthropic or OpenAI cut those default spend caps.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Watch the Senate on the China hosting bill, CoreWeave's remaining prepayments, and whether Anthropic files or prices around November nineteenth.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's ARA AI News. We'll be back when the picture changes.
